title: Planning sustainable places

draft.title: Planning sustainable places
card: A sustainable place meets the needs of people today without harming the environment or the needs of future generations. A liveable place is one where people can enjoy a good quality of life. Planners work to achieve both.
building more homes within existing urban areas, such as units near train stations. It can reduce urban sprawl and make better use of roads, pipes and services already built.
trains, buses and light rail. Good services can give people an option other than driving, which can reduce traffic and emissions.
parks, trees and waterways can cool a place and give people room to relax. Good design, such as walkable streets and a mix of homes, shops and jobs close together, can cut the need for long trips.
draft.remember: Planners combine denser housing, public transport, green space and good design to make places more sustainable and liveable.

a.q: A council allows more apartments to be built near an existing train station, instead of clearing bushland on the city edge. Which planning approach is this?
a.why: Building more homes within an existing urban area is urban consolidation. Green space provision is the most tempting wrong option, but the council is adding housing, not parks.
a.clue: Where are the new homes being built: inside or outside the existing city?

b.q: A planner in a growing outer suburb wants to reduce car use and make daily life easier for residents. Which proposal is most likely to do this?
opts: Put shops, jobs and homes close together on walkable streets
Build wider roads so that car trips are faster
Place new housing far from town centres to keep lots large
Build one large shopping centre away from the suburb
b.why: A mix of homes, shops and jobs within walking distance means many trips become short enough to walk or cycle, which can cut car use. Wider roads are the tempting option, but they can make driving easier and so can encourage more car trips.
b.clue: Which option makes everyday destinations closer to home?

b.best: Put shops, jobs and homes close together on walkable streets
